digest.component_or_area: store reconciliation / git union-merge in sync.py
propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and renames sources to *.retired without atomic rollback, leaving the tracker working tree dirty when the detached sweep is interrupted.

The next reconverge _union_merge fails with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' when origin has introduced those same paths via a peer's push, and the abort-only handler cannot recover.
Every reconverge retry re-aborts identically because git reset --hard ignores untracked files and _stash_create lacks -u flag, creating a permanent wedge that strands local commits off origin.
The fix detects the specific untracked-overwrite abort signature, parses the exact paths git names, relocates only those paths to git-common-dir/reconverge-quarantine/, and retries the merge once.
On merge retry success, origin's authoritative versions are pulled in and both parents are kept, preserving all local commits and breaking the wedge without data loss.
